history.summary: GENERIC-NAME FLAG: 'Ramar Temple' matches several shrines across Coimbatore district (Mettupalayam Road, Kariyagoundanur, Ondipudur and others). This file documents the most prominent one: the Ram Nagar temple at Sapthagiri Towers, 10A Ramar Koil Street, Ram Nagar, Coimbatore 641009, near Gandhipuram bus stand. The Dravidian-style temple is noted for its idols of Rama and Sita facing each other (symbolising their devotion), with Lakshmana in the sanctum; some guides also claim it is the only temple where Rama and Anjaneya face each other - conflicting claims, verify. The gopuram is described as levelled with colourful sculptures, the doors covered with silver sheets carrying carvings of the eight avatars of Lakshmi, and the complex reportedly houses 13 crore Rama-namas; there are also shrines to Ganesha, Krishna, Aiyappa and the navagrahas. If the CSV intended a different Ramar temple, this file may need re-targeting.

town_description: Coimbatore is a major industrial city in western Tamil Nadu at the foot of the Western Ghats, often called the 'Manchester of South India'. Ram Nagar is a central locality near Gandhipuram bus stand, a short distance from Coimbatore Junction railway station, with several long-established Hindu temples.
